summary:
We developed Lunar South Pole Site Navigator, an interactive mission-planning web application and explainable AI pipeline for evaluating NASA CLPS and Artemis III landing sites. Because the Moon has no atmosphere and only a 1.54-degree axial tilt, steep crater rims near the South Pole create extreme variations in solar power and Direct-to-Earth communication across locations and launch dates.

Our tool addresses this challenge by combining a FastAPI physics engine, an HTML5 Canvas dashboard, and an auditable machine learning pipeline. Users can drop pins on a South Pole stereographic map, test +7d and +14d launch delays, scrub a 708-hour lunar day, inspect 360° terrain horizon clipping with Time to Sunset and Time to Earthset countdowns, and compare sites side-by-side. By pairing monotonic XGBoost suitability scores with 90% confidence intervals, safety gates, and TreeSHAP feature attributions, the tool accelerates agile mission planning while remaining accessible to educators and the public.
details: Lunar South Pole Site Navigator is an interactive mission-planning and educational tool built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It combines a FastAPI physics engine (curvature-corrected LOLA horizons, Lambertian solar irradiance, Stefan-Boltzmann thermal equilibrium, and Friis Direct-to-Earth link margins), an explainable offline ML pipeline (8×8 Kohonen SOM terrain clustering, monotonic-constrained XGBoost suitability scoring, 90% conformal prediction intervals, and native TreeSHAP attributions), and a zero-build HTML5 Canvas dashboard to rapidly compare candidate landing sites and launch dates.
